findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify the 'DET-block short-circuit' story's intended scope: if the goal is only to avoid redundant LLM spend when DET already blocks, specify which DET criteria skip LLM vs which still run it for advisory/coaching value, and add a positive rationale explaining why the selected criteria's DET block alone is sufficient for authors to revise without LLM context.
evidence: workflow_ops.py:208-219: 'A P1/P5 DET block does NOT stop the LLM — bespoke still runs the four-pass review and MERGES the DET blocks at decide-time. So: P8-too-big → short-circuit (ELSE arm): a BLOCK verdict from the DET blocks, no LLM. any other DET block (P1/P5) → run the LLM (THEN arm)'
Plan Decomposition: 'DET-block short-circuit' listed as 'Independent stories/tasks' without rationale for abandoning the intentional P1/P5 LLM-merge design

Success Criteria: 'No gate weakening: the criteria enabled for blocking ... use the operator-approved thresholds, and all previously blocking criteria remain blocking' — dropping advisory/coaching from DET-blocked plans is a form of gate weakening not covered by the threshold clause
ABSENCE: the plan provides no positive rationale for why skipping LLM on all DET blocks is preferable to the current design that merges DET+LLM findings
findings.finding: The 'DET-block short-circuit' story proposes widening the P8 short-circuit to ALL DET blocks, but the current code explicitly and intentionally lets P1/P5 DET blocks still run the LLM so that LLM-sourced advisories and coaching merge into the verdict (workflow_ops.py:208-219, comment: 'A P1/P5 DET block does NOT stop the LLM — bespoke still runs the four-pass review and MERGES the DET blocks at decide-time'). Widening to skip the LLM on any DET block drops that advisory+coaching from blocked plans, which may violate the Success Criterion 'No gate weakening'. The plan provides no positive rationale for this trade-off and does not address the advisory/coaching loss.
findings.location: Decomposition section ('DET-block short-circuit' story) and Success Criteria ('No gate weakening')
scenarios: A plan with a P1 clarity block (e.g. missing verification hook) currently still gets LLM advisory findings explaining WHAT is missing and HOW to fix it; after the change it gets only the DET block, losing actionable coaching that helps the author revise efficiently.

A P5 DET block (plan too large but not P8-too-big) currently still produces advisory findings from the LLM review; widening to skip LLM removes those, giving the author less signal to reduce the plan's size correctly.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict the short-circuit to criteria where the DET finding alone is prescriptive enough for revision (e.g. P8-too-big, where the fix is always 'reduce plan size') and explicitly keep the LLM running for P1/P5 blocks where author needs advisory detail. Document this as a per-criterion short-circuit policy rather than a blanket 'all DET blocks'.

findings.location: Ticket 696a comment 3: 'G7 = strongest blocking case... blocking for contradicts_reality @0.80-0.85; unresolvable parent → abstain not finding; closed-parent rule'
scenarios: An executor changes G7's block_threshold and default_posture in criteria_routing.json but omits the abstain/closed-parent rule from the rubric prompt — the LLM fires a blocking finding on a leaf whose parent ticket is closed or cannot be fetched, producing false blocks
The 'closed-parent rule' is interpreted differently by the rubric author vs. the orchestrator, producing inconsistent behavior
